Students from JVHS, row 1, farthest to the left, Stella Simpson, Maggie Barton, Farrah Norris; row 2, Harper Boyd, Chloe Borst, Liam Lightner, and Jackson Kline, work in the computer lab.

Did you know that 70% of adults are more worried about AI than excited about it, and about two-thirds feel AI carries high societal risks? As technology progresses in daily life and the school system, artificial intelligence continues to become even more integrated into the function of every school system. Juniata Valley High School is no exception.

Artificial intelligence is a computer program or a machine that is automated to create what normally requires human intelligence. One of Juniata Valley’s business educators, Darren Boyd, stated that “AI is changing education by creating both opportunities and challenges for students and teachers.” Because of the help of AI when it comes to teaching material and the classroom and learning, the students and teachers are now experiencing a way of learning that is unprecedented.
